hub.title: Tutorials
hub.blurb: Short playable lessons. No synced catalog required. Complete any lesson to mark it done on this device.

steps.title: Win condition
steps.body:
[b]North Star[/b] is a competitive card game. Your long-term goal is to earn [b]5 stars[/b] for your restaurant before your opponent does.

Stars usually come from winning [b]Faceoffs[/b] (we cover that in a later lesson).

steps.title: Three piles
steps.body:
You bring three things to a match:

• [b]Chef[/b] — sets your baseline [b]influence[/b] each round and which restaurant types fit your plan.
• [b]Restaurant deck[/b] — several restaurant cards; you will pick one to run during the match.
• [b]Main deck[/b] — staff, meals, events, and support that you draw and play during rounds.

steps.title: Check
steps.body:
Which pile gives you your baseline influence each Setup round?

Pick [b]Chef[/b] when you are ready to continue.

steps.title: Before the match
steps.body: After shuffling your [b]restaurant deck[/b], you may look at the [b]top[/b] and [b]bottom[/b] cards. Pick one to be your [b]active restaurant[/b] for the game (unless an effect swaps it later).

steps.title: Try it
steps.body: Below are two sample restaurants. Choose [b]Top[/b] or [b]Bottom[/b]. Your choice only affects this lesson.

steps.title: Opening hand
steps.body: You start with [b]5[/b] cards. Before the first round begins, you may take [b]one[/b] mulligan: [b]all five[/b] cards go back, you shuffle, and you draw a fresh five. You cannot mulligan individual cards.

steps.title: Practice
steps.body: Tap [b]Mulligan all[/b] to return all five and redraw, or [b]Keep hand[/b] to continue. This uses a tiny demo deck in memory only.

steps.title: Simultaneous setup
steps.body: Each [b]Setup[/b], you draw up to at least [b]5[/b] cards, then you may [b]set[/b] cards face-down in a line up to your [b]influence[/b]. You must fix illegal placements before you lock — the game will not let you lock an illegal board.

steps.title: Food & support
steps.body: [b]Meals (food)[/b] can be set face-down in your line during Setup like other cards (they attach to your restaurant when revealed in Faceoff, up to [b]3[/b] foods). [b]Support[/b] is not set in the line — you play it from hand when rules allow.

steps.title: Try it
steps.body: Spend influence to add [b]Staff[/b], [b]Meal[/b], or [b]Event[/b] from your demo hand. [b]Support[/b] stays disabled here on purpose. Remove the last placed card if you need to adjust.

steps.title: Reveal order
steps.body: In a Faceoff, hidden cards reveal [b]left to right[/b]. Meal cards you placed can attach to your restaurant (up to [b]3[/b] foods). Your score is [b]base restaurant rating[/b] plus [b]food ratings[/b] from attached meals.

steps.title: Stars
steps.body: Higher total wins the Faceoff and gains a star. On a [b]tie[/b], [b]both[/b] players gain a star. If both hit [b]5+[/b] stars on the same update, the match is a [b]draw[/b]. Stars can go down from effects and never below [b]0[/b].

steps.title: Demo totals
steps.body: Press [b]Show demo scores[/b] to compare two sample boards using the same rating fields as the desktop sim.

steps.title: Deck rules
steps.body:
From the main menu, open [b]Deck building[/b] to build a legal loadout:

• Main deck: exactly [b]30[/b] cards from staff / meal / event / support, max [b]3[/b] copies of the same card.
• Restaurant deck: [b]3–10[/b] unique restaurants.
• One chef.

CPU matches also check chef vs restaurant types using catalog fields.

steps.title: Next step
steps.body: When you are comfortable, try [b]CPU matches[/b] with a saved deck. Good luck!
